profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company, traded as NVDA, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, USA. Its most recent 10-K, covering a period ending 2026-01-25, reported revenue of $215,938,000,000. The company's site presents its AI work through the NVIDIA Nemotron family of multimodal models, which the company describes as open models built for long-running, self-evolving agents and for agentic reasoning in graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. The site names Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, as sharing the vision behind Nemotron.

The company describes Nemotron models as openly available, with published training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. Named components include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for specialized tasks, NeMo Switchyard for routing each step to the right model, Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding and embeddings. Deployment runs through NVIDIA NIM microservices, which require an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license and are available from build.nvidia.com, alongside NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Blueprints, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TensorRT-LLM, with support for open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM and for NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware. The site also cites work with partners across the ecosystem, including ServiceNow on visual question-and-answer accuracy.

The company's litigation exposure is recorded as 281 cases in California, with no individual cases listed. No MCP servers are recorded for it.
